text:
maya: Heads up — after PTQ bringup of v2-reranker I see a weird shape in ndcg vs. per-query-noise. Not just a single drop, more like a floor appears for short queries. Posting quick plot summary and artifacts. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: Can you paste the eval command and the exact model/quant flags?

maya: Ran: `./eval_rerank.sh --model rbrk-v2-small --quant int8-awq --dataset webqa-holdout --seed 42 --batch 128`

maya: Quick CSV tail: `query_len,ndcg@10,mrr
1,0.41,0.28
2,0.57,0.39
3,0.68,0.45
4,0.72,0.47` — baseline fp16 numbers are `1->0.63,2->0.68` so short queries lost a lot.

omar: Oof. That's the classic short-query noisefloor. Two quick suspects: tokenizer truncation/segmentation differences after quant pack, or candidate ordering (determinism) regressing.

lee: Any difference in candidate pooling? If negative mining changed ranks, nDCG can look like a floor for qlen=1.

maya: Candidate pool same. I compared topk source and it's identical listwise for a sample of 200 queries.

ana: @maya can you dump tokenized example for qlen=1 case? Need to check token ids and priming tokens length.

maya: Here’s one sample: ```
query: "ipython"
tokens: [314, 87, 2]
priming: "Search: " (tokens len 2)
context concat: query + priming -> results in extra prefix token after quant pack?
```

sam: Hmm token ids look same. Did you use dynamic padding/batching changes? PTQ can change KV cache alignment and effective context if we accidentally shifted priming insertion.

maya: Batch code unchanged. But I noticed we switched to the new runtime op `kvpack-v3` which behaves slightly differently for zero-length segments. Could that matter?

omar: It can. If kvpack offsets are off-by-one for short sequences it will noise the logits for first few tokens — which disproportionately affects short queries.

lee: Can we reproduce in CPU FP32 with same runtime path? If it's runtime bug, fp32 path with same kvpack should show similar pattern.

maya: I ran FP32 on the same runtime (no quant) — no drop. So seems quant + runtime combo.

ana: Two experiments: 1) run int8 with old kvpack (v2) 2) run AWQ but with explicit zero-pad to length 4 before priming to see if alignment avoids floor.

maya: Kicking both off now. CI bot: @ci-bot started job rerank-eval/1748625301-a (old-kvpack-int8) and rerank-eval/1748625301-b (pad-to-4-int8)

ci-bot: Job rerank-eval/1748625301-a queued. Job rerank-eval/1748625301-b queued.

sam: Also add a tiny test: compute pairwise rank flip rate between fp16 and int8 for qlen=1. If flip rate >> expected then quantization noise is changing ordering not just scores.

maya: Flip-rate for sample 1000 qlen=1 queries: 0.38. Baseline acceptable ~0.08 on other lengths. So high.

omar: Confirms ordering instability. I suspect per-head scaling in AWQ interacting with fused rotary kernels in kvpack-v3.

lee: If true, workaround might be to disable per-head scale for final dense in PTQ for small models; or tweak scale clipping. Both cheap.

maya: Results: old-kvpack-int8 job finished — ndcg@10 for qlen=1 = 0.60 (close to fp16). pad-to-4-int8 finished = 0.59. So alignment workaround restores quality.

sam: Great. So root cause likely kvpack-v3 offset interpretation with compressed int8 kv tensors.

ana: Action items: 1) Omar to triage kvpack-v3+int8 path and add unit test for zero-length segments (owner: omar) 2) Lee to run a small PTQ config sweep disabling per-head scales and measure flip-rate (owner: lee) 3) Maya to pin runtime to v2 for tonight's canary deploy and add a note to bringup doc (owner: maya)

omar: Filed GH issue: redwood/runtime#1234 with reproducer and sample token dumps.

lee: I'll run per-head off sweep tomorrow morning and post summary.

maya: Thanks everyone. Leaving this thread with final note: short-query NDCG floors are a good canary — add qlen=1/2 slice to our CI smokebench for future onboards. :white_check_mark:
